chapterTitle: Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 1 (FBISE Class 12 Chemistry)
title: Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 1 (FBISE Class 12 Chemistry)
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: Which of the following elements exhibits the highest first ionization energy?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest nuclear charge among Period 2 reactive nonmetals with a small atomic radius, requiring the most energy to remove an electron.

questions.question: Beryllium differs from other alkaline earth metals because it:

options.A: Forms predominantly covalent compounds due to high polarizing power (small Be²⁺ size)
options.D: Has the lowest ionization energy in Group IIA

questions.explanation: Tiny Be²⁺ has immense charge density, polarizing anions and conferring high covalent character to its compounds (Fajans' rule).

questions.question: The exceptional hardness and high melting point (>3500°C) of diamond is attributed to:

options.A: Van der Waals forces between graphene layers
options.B: Giant three-dimensional tetrahedral network of sp³-hybridized carbon atoms linked by strong covalent bonds

questions.explanation: Every carbon in diamond is sp³ hybridized, bonded tetrahedrally to 4 other carbons in an interlocking 3D covalent lattice.

questions.question: Which oxide of nitrogen is known as 'laughing gas' and used as a mild anesthetic?
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide (N₂O) produces euphoria and hysterical laughter upon inhalation and is used in dental anesthesia.

questions.question: Which noble gas is radioactive, produced as a daughter decay product of Radium-226?
questions.explanation: Radon-222 is an alpha-emitting noble gas resulting from the radioactive decay of Ra-226 in rock and soil.

questions.question: What is the geometry and hybridization of the diamagnetic nickel complex [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻?
questions.explanation: CN⁻ is a strong field ligand that forces pairing of Ni²⁺ (3d⁸) electrons, freeing one 3d orbital for dsp² hybridization and square planar geometry.

questions.question: Molecules that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other are called:
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are chiral stereoisomers that rotate plane-polarized light in equal magnitudes but opposite directions (dextro and levo).

questions.question: When ethyne (acetylene) gas is passed through ammoniacal cuprous chloride (Cu₂Cl₂) solution, a characteristic precipitate of which color is formed?
questions.explanation: HC≡CH + 2 [Cu(NH₃)₂]⁺ → Cu-C≡C-Cu↓ (red ppt of dicopper acetylide) + 2 NH₄⁺ + 2 NH₃.

questions.question: In the presence of bright sunlight (UV light) and in the absence of a halogen carrier, benzene reacts with chlorine by addition to produce:
questions.explanation: C₆H₆ + 3 Cl₂ xrightarrow{UV light} C₆H₆Cl₆ (1,2,3,4,5,6-hexachlorocyclohexane, commercially called Gammexane or Lindane, an agricultural insecticide).

questions.question: When a Grignard reagent (R-Mg-X) is bubbled with dry Carbon Dioxide (CO₂) followed by acid hydrolysis, the organic product is:
questions.explanation: R-MgX + O=C=O → R-COO⁻MgX⁺ xrightarrow{H₃O⁺} R-COOH (carboxylic acid with one more carbon than R).

questions.question: Williamson Ether Synthesis involves an S_N2 displacement between:

options.A: A sodium alkoxide (R-O⁻Na⁺) and an unhindered primary alkyl halide (R'-X)
options.B: Two alcohol molecules with conc. H₂SO₄

questions.explanation: R-ONa + R'X → R-O-R' + NaX. Primary alkyl halides give high ether yields via backside S_N2 attack; tertiary halides undergo E2 elimination instead.

questions.question: Formalin, an aqueous solution widely used to preserve biological specimens and embalm tissues, contains approximately:

options.A: 37% to 40% Formaldehyde (methanal) in water with ~10% methanol stabilizer

questions.explanation: Commercial formalin is 37-40% aqueous formaldehyde stabilized with 8-10% methanol to prevent precipitation of insoluble paraformaldehyde polymer.

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for Phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid)?
questions.explanation: Phthalic acid is ortho-benzene-dicarboxylic acid: Benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid.

questions.question: The sugar unit present in the backbone of RNA is β-D-ribose, whereas DNA contains:
questions.explanation: DNA contains 2'-deoxyribose, which has -H instead of -OH at the C-2' position, conferring greater chemical stability against alkaline hydrolysis.

questions.question: The Fourdrinier machine is the heart of a paper mill, performing which continuous sequence of operations?

options.A: Forming the wet web on a moving wire mesh screen, dewatering by suction, pressing, drying on heated steam cylinders, and calendering

questions.explanation: A dilute 0.5% pulp suspension flows onto a moving endless wire cloth, draining water and consolidating into a continuous paper sheet.

questions.question: A shift of an absorption band toward longer wavelength (lower energy) is known as a:
questions.explanation: Bathochromic (red) shift moves λ_max to longer wavelengths; hypsochromic (blue) shift moves λ_max to shorter wavelengths.

questions.question: Which of the following is a nucleophile?
questions.explanation: Ammonia has an unshared lone pair of electrons on nitrogen available for donation to electron-deficient centers, functioning as a nucleophile.
